🚀 VSCoder Copilot – Code Smarter, Anywhere

Turn your phone into an AI-powered coding companion. VSCoder Copilot brings the full power of GitHub Copilot and seamless VS Code remote editing directly to your mobile device. Review, edit, and build projects anytime — no complex setup required.

✨ Features

🌍 Code from anywhere
Securely connect your phone to VS Code across home, office, or mobile networks. No port forwarding or VPN needed.

🤖 Full GitHub Copilot on mobile
Get AI-powered code suggestions, explanations, and completions right inside the app.

📂 Edit your projects remotely
Browse and edit your entire VS Code workspace from your phone with real-time sync.

⚡ Instant setup

Install the extension in VS Code

Start the VSCoder server

Pair your mobile app with a 6-digit code

Start coding instantly

🔒 Secure pairing
Connections are temporary, private, and protected by time-limited pairing codes.

💡 Perfect for

Code reviews on the go

Debugging during commute or travel

Quick fixes without your laptop

Remote dev workflows with Copilot

Why developers love VSCoder Copilot

Fast & lightweight: Optimized for mobile performance.

Simple & secure: No firewall hassle or risky setups.

Boost productivity: AI + remote access = smarter coding.

👉 Whether you’re a student, hobbyist, or professional developer, VSCoder Copilot helps you keep coding wherever you are.

quotes.text:
Hi All,

Over time I built a small set of Android apps, mostly single-purpose utilities and one
developer-focused companion tool.

Utility apps (no accounts, no subscriptions):
- Offline PDF & EPUB reader/editor
- QR & barcode scanner and generator
- Phone hardware and battery diagnostics

Developer tool:
- VSCoder Copilot – a mobile companion for VS Code / GitHub Copilot workflows

For the utility apps, the focus was:
- minimal permissions
- no background services
- all on-device processing

VSCoder is different by nature and supports optional paid features.

I’d appreciate feedback, especially on UX decisions, permission discipline, and whether
there’s still room for focused utility software on Android.

Google Play links:

PDF & EPUB Reader–Editor
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.pdfepub.readereditor

QR & Barcode Scanner
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.emirbaycan.qrbarcode.scanner

Phone Health Checker
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.phonehealthcheckernew

VSCoder Copilot
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.emirbaycan.vscodercopilot
